source.title: When Are Sparse Feature Interventions Actually Localized? Matched Evaluation for SAE-Based Safety Control

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Page breaks and a few formatting artifacts do not prevent reading the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The study constructs a refusal direction from differences in mean activations and evaluates related activation interventions, but it does not remove the single direction by projecting it out at every layer and position. It instead compares ranked SAE feature ablations with dense steering, including matched-surface and matched-basis baselines.
record.gate_note: The study reports intervention outcomes relevant to refusal-related harmful compliance and capability. The refusal direction's construction is described as a method, not itself a result row. Feature-ranking statistics and projection coverage are diagnostics rather than outcomes of the claimed refusal intervention; they are not rows here. The authors cite prior work on a single refusal direction, but cited results are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study builds a difference-in-means refusal direction from refused minus complied harmful prompts. It reports what subtracting it does to coherent harmful compliance (9B, 27B, 2B, Llama) and what adding it does to harmful compliance, with capability, on Gemma-2-9B. These are steering interventions, not directional ablation, and the direction is a dense baseline for the paper's SAE comparison. Most rows record SAE-minus-dense differences, which do not bear on V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that SAE localization claims depend on dense-baseline matching: on Gemma-2-9B, the advantage over all-layer dense steering reverses against same-layer and decoder-span dense baselines under both judges. The advantage over all-layer dense remains large on Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-27B. In 2B, SAE jailbreaks are judge inflation with capability collapse. Dense steering is the more capability-preserving tool for refusal injection.
record.recipe_differences: The study constructs a difference-in-means refusal direction and tests activation interventions, but its main removal intervention ablates ranked SAE features at one layer rather than projecting one direction out of every layer and position. It also tests dense direction addition, not the original harmless-request refusal measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with dense-baseline matching (all-layer versus same-layer or decoder-span projected), model scale and architecture, SAE feature count, perturbation strength, and direction of intervention (removal versus refusal injection).

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating SAE features ranked by alignment with the refusal direction raises coherent jailbreak. It beats all-layer dense steering per unit perturbation (9B, Llama, 27B) but loses to same-layer and decoder-span dense steering on 9B. No single feature exceeds 0.04 jailbreak. In 2B the effect is single-judge inflation with capability collapse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features aligned with the refusal direction offer a more perturbation-efficient refusal-removal handle than dense steering.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says a public artifact will be released and that materials are available from the authors on request.
record.problems: The study does not directly perform the claimed all-layer single-direction ablation. Llama and 27B comparisons use all-layer dense baselines rather than the surface-matched baselines; 27B has three seeds, 4-bit weights, and no comparable capability results. The human audit is targeted and single-annotator. The second-judge template is described as slightly off-specification for the in-the-wild prompt source used on 2B and Llama. The perturbation metric is acknowledged to be a proxy for locality, not proof of causal isolation.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted some auxiliary numeric outcomes to stay focused on the claim: the remaining raw Table 2 model-method metrics; full matched-target-effect Table 3 comparisons; the other Table 5 HarmBench per-method rates; the individual layer-scan capability values in Table 6; additional Table 8 coherence and perturbation values; Table 10 MMLU, GSM8K, and XSTest results; full Table 11 judge rates for other settings; the human audit counts; the single-feature ablation maximum and mean effects; and the full Table 12 intermediate capability values. These are reported in Sections 5.1–5.6 and Tables 2–12.

untested.parts: Directional ablation (projecting the direction out at every layer and position). A harmful-minus-harmless construction: they use refused-minus-complied harmful prompts. Inducing refusal on harmless prompts.
No weight edit or abliterated released model.
No analysis of jailbreak mechanisms or adversarial training.
No test of affine, cone, or multi-direction structure; SAE feature distribution is a different construct.
Directions are built per model; no transfer test.

missing.what: Dense refusal-direction addition: harmful compliance 0.908 baseline → 0.363/0.291/0.227/0.181/0.142 at perturbation 0.24–0.47
9B all-layer dense removal at default strength: true jailbreak 0.3146, MMLU 0.628 vs baseline 0.680, coherence 1.0
9B same-layer dense (layer 20) true jailbreak 0.170/0.221/0.496 (Guard), 0.164/0.203/0.382 (HarmBench), at β 0.16/0.20/0.31, coherence 1.0; projected dense 0.142/0.200/0.414
Llama-3.1-8B dense steering true jailbreak only 0.057 at β 0.60 (perturbation 0.77)
Dense gated jailbreak rates: 2B dense β 0.15 0.423 Guard / 0.363 HB; 9B dense β 0.05 0.038 / 0.025

record.verdict_notes: The study is about SAE localization; the Arditi refusal direction is cited and serves as the dense baseline. Its direction is refused-minus-complied harmful prompts, applied by additive steering rather than projection ablation, so V1 evidence is indirect. Most extracted rows are SAE-versus-dense differences and were relinked to none. Rows r23–r25 were mislabeled as addition.

versions.untested_parts: Does not project out the single difference-in-means direction at every layer and position. Does not report refusal rates on harmless requests after adding the direction. The tested feature ablations are multi-feature interventions, not removal of one direction.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration experiment.
Does not test whether jailbreak attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Feature-rank diagnostics and the single-feature ablation do not test whether refusal is represented by an affine set, cone, or multiple directions.
The study compares safety and behavior-completion judges, but does not test whether harmfulness judgment is separately encoded from refusal decision.
Uses separately constructed directions across model configurations; does not test transfer of a direction across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Does not vary refusal-training method or timing.
GSM8K is used as a capability measure, but no reasoning model is evaluated.

relationships.condition: Gemma-2-9B-it, dense addition of the refusal direction on harmful-compliance prompts
relationships.reason: Harmful compliance falls from 0.908 to 0.142 at perturbation 0.47 while GSM8K (0.677 vs 0.700) and MMLU (0.677 vs 0.692) stay near flat (r41, r42; compliance values from Table 12 text, see missing).
relationships.display_finding: At perturbation 0.47, harmful compliance fell from 0.908 to 0.142, while GSM8K scored 0.677 versus 0.700 and MMLU scored 0.677 versus 0.692.

relationships.condition: Gemma-2-27B-it (4-bit), all-layer dense subtraction of the direction
relationships.reason: Coherent jailbreak reaches only 0.433 from 0.006 at β 0.05; stronger β collapses coherence (0.163, 0.056), so removal is incomplete and costs abilities (r23–r25).
relationships.display_finding: For 4-bit Gemma-2-27B-it, all-layer dense subtraction increased coherent jailbreak from 0.006 to only 0.433 at β=0.05, while stronger settings reduced coherence to 0.163 and 0.056.

relationships.condition: Gemma-2-9B-it, dense subtraction (all-layer and layer-20 only)
relationships.reason: From text, no row: all-layer dense reaches true jailbreak 0.31 with MMLU 0.628 vs 0.680; same-layer reaches 0.496 at β 0.31. Refusal is removed only partly.
relationships.display_finding: For Gemma-2-9B-it, all-layer subtraction achieved true jailbreak of 0.31 while MMLU fell from 0.680 to 0.628; layer-20 subtraction achieved 0.496 at β=0.31.

relationships.condition: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, all-layer dense subtraction of the direction
relationships.reason: From text, no row: dense steering yields true jailbreak of only 0.057 even at β 0.60 (perturbation 0.77). Steering rather than projection ablation, so the test differs from the original.
relationships.display_finding: The true jailbreak rate reached only 0.057 even at β=0.60 with perturbation 0.77; the intervention used steering rather than projection ablation.
